**UI-for-ytdlp v0.3.7** adds an opt-in anonymized download journal so two runs can be compared by server, format, and speed.

#### Verbose download log
- Off by default. Enable **Подробный журнал загрузки** in Settings; the choice is saved.
- While the journal is open, yt-dlp receives `--verbose`, `--print-traffic`, and `--progress-delta 1`. `--dump-pages` and `--print` are not used.
- Each run writes `utilities/logs/download-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.log`. Every line has a timestamp.
- The window shows stages, not HTTP traffic. URLs, titles, video ids, account names, cookies, and user paths are removed from both the window and the file.
- The summary separates page parse, download, ffmpeg re-encode, and merge. Format includes itag, height, codecs, container, and size.
- Bytes read by ffmpeg are counted per TCP host. HTTP status is left blank when ffmpeg does not print it.
- Average speed uses those network bytes, not the size of the finished file.
- ffmpeg banners and libx264 statistics stay out of the file. The progress bar ignores libx264 percentages and only follows `[download]` lines.

#### Validation
- A 12-second YouTube download through the ffmpeg downloader produced a 4.2s page parse, 10.7s download, 7.1s encode, and format `135+140, 480p, h264+aac`.
- Cookies, the video id, and the title stayed out of the log and the window. The progress bar did not jump on libx264 output.
- Unit tests cover redaction, the ffmpeg summary, and progress parsing.

#### Downloads
- **Installer:** `UI-for-ytdlp-0.3.7-windows-x64-setup.exe`
- **Portable ZIP:** `UI-for-ytdlp-0.3.7-windows-x64.zip`
- **Standalone executable:** `UI-for-ytdlp.exe`
